newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Italy wants Security Council to speed up oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Italy wants Security Council to speed up oil deal.

text.p: Italy wants the Security Council to make clear that Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali should go ahead with the oil-for-food deal in Iraq despite the latest upheavals in the north.
To this end it will introduce a statement in the council on Tuesday asking Boutros-Ghali to procede as soon as possible in implementing the plan, an Italian spokesman said.
"Everyone seems to forget that there are people starving and dying," said Sebastiano Cardi.
Boutros-Ghali has put the plan on hold, fearing for the safety of U.N. staff, President Clinton has said that the United States would determine when the plan could move forward again.
Several diplomats said that they would probably agree to a statement that would ask Boutros-Ghali to procede as soon as he deems that conditions permit.

Last Tuesday, Clinton, explaining why he unleashed cruise missiles against Iraq, said that "until we are sure these humanitarian supplies can actually get to those who need them, the plan cannot go forward."

But to date neither the United Nations nor the United States is saying when the plan would be implemented. American envoys have pointed out that with Iraq assuming control over large areas of the north, some adjustment is needed.
The plan originally forsaw the United Nations being in charge of food distribution to the Kurdish north without Baghdad's interference.

The deal, signed on May 20, allows Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to raise funds for food, medicine and other supplies for civilians suffering under six years of trade sanctions.
